attacks.claim: Plan moves chunks and embeddings of customer documents into Nimbus Vector Store, which is provisioned in us-east-2. This directly violates the DPA constraint that all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) be processed and stored in the EU. EU regions are only a roadmap item with no date.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap." and Week 2: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store"

attacks.claim: EU law-firm client data (privileged legal content, embeddings derived from it) would be transferred to the US with no transfer mechanism, DPIA, or customer notification. ZDR addendum covers the Inference API, not the Vector Store, which persists data by design.
attacks.evidence: ZDR ref NMB-ZDR-2291 is cited only under Generation; Vector Store storage region us-east-2; ABSENT: any transfer assessment or subprocessor/customer notice.

attacks.claim: Quality parity is claimed from 25 hand-picked support-inbox questions judged by two staff lawyers, with 3 of 25 not preferred. This is not evidence of parity across 4,100 cases and practice areas, especially after replacing LoRA adapters with untested system prompts.
attacks.evidence: "This confirms quality parity or better, so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+)"

attacks.claim: The agreed constraint makes the 4,100-case regression suite the release gate for any model change, yet the plan cuts all tenants over in week 4 and runs the suite only in week 6+, after cutover. This inverts the gate.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over" vs "Week 6+: regression suite run, prompt tuning on any failures."

attacks.claim: Week 3 releases the GPU reservation and deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters before cutover (week 4) and before any eval. This destroys the rollback path and the fine-tuned IP, which is irrecoverable. Week 5 also removes pgvector and the vLLM manifests.
attacks.evidence: "Week 3: release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: There is no rollback, canary, or staged tenant rollout; all tenants are cut over at once with no fallback once the old stack is gone. Dependence on a public-preview Vector Store (no SLA stated) for the retrieval hot path is risky, and the plan has no monitoring or alerting for the new dependency.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)." and "Vector Store is in public preview"

attacks.claim: Complete dependence on a single vendor for generation, embeddings, and retrieval, with the fine-tuned weights deleted and pgvector removed. Exit cost is very high: re-embedding 41M chunks and re-creating the fine-tuning. Embeddings (1,536 dims, vendor-specific) are not portable.
attacks.evidence: "Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector"; "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters"

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation rests on per-tenant collections and keys in a preview product, described as 'mirroring' pgvector schemas without verification. The plan does not address how tenant-scoped keys are provisioned or stored for the 41M-chunk multi-tenant corpus, or any isolation testing, which matters for privileged legal data.
attacks.evidence: "one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key, mirroring today's per-tenant pgvector schemas"

attacks.claim: Cost table omits migration-period double-running costs (GPU is held through week 3, with dual-write), the one-time cost of re-embedding 41M chunks, and the effect of 200k context on token spend. The generation estimate of $7,900 has no stated basis. The savings are asserted without data.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) $7,900"; ABSENT: token volume assumptions or re-embedding cost

attacks.claim: Rate-limit headroom is given only in req/s, while long-context (up to 200k) requests are typically bound by tokens-per-minute quotas, which are not addressed. A 41M-chunk re-embed in week 2 may also hit embedding quotas.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s"

attacks.claim: Per-practice system prompts are drafted in week 1 with no versioning or testing plan, and replace fine-tuned adapters. Behavior drift is untracked.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts"
